name: Berezina
summary: With Chichagov holding the far bank at Borisov and Wittgenstein and Kutuzov closing behind, the Grande Armée was trapped against the Berezina. A feint drew Chichagov south while Eblé's pontonniers, standing in the icy river, built two bridges at Studienka. For three days the army crossed, Oudinot and Ney holding off Chichagov in the woods on the right bank and Victor holding the heights on the left against Wittgenstein, until the bridges were burned on the 29th with thousands of stragglers still on the far side.

forces.name: Legrand's Division
forces.summary: Oudinot's leading division across the bridges on the 26th, which drove back Chaplits's men and held the woods at Stakhov on the right bank on the 28th; Legrand was wounded.
notes: By late November every formation was a fraction of the strength in Nafziger's returns; mark battalions Small or leave some out to suit.
After Nafziger's return of the II Corps for 15 September 1812.
Each regiment had its own two or four 3-pdrs, shown as Regimental Artillery.
The horse battery, without the three cavalry regiments the list wants for it, shows as a historical departure.

forces.name: Corbineau's and Doumerc's Cavalry
forces.formation: II Corps cavalry and 3rd Cuirassier Division
forces.summary: On the 28th Doumerc's cuirassiers, a few hundred men, charged through the woods into Chichagov's infantry, breaking several battalions and taking 2,000 prisoners, the last great charge of the campaign.
notes: By late November every formation was a fraction of the strength in Nafziger's returns; mark battalions Small or leave some out to suit.
After Nafziger's return of the II Corps for 15 September 1812. The light regiments were down to two to four hundred men each, so they are Small, as is the 7th Cuirassiers.
Doumerc's three brigades of one regiment each are shown together.
Cavalry without infantry, two light brigades and the second horse battery show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.
